citations.description: Ticket comments reviewed via show_ticket: comment 1 is the seam analysis (no pytest output); comment 2 is '--body-file' (no pytest output). No pytest summary lines appear anywhere in the ticket.

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus any new seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines in a comment
findings.detail: The ticket has only two comments: the seam analysis comment (planning/analysis text, no pytest output) and a bare '--body-file' comment. Neither contains pytest summary lines. The required concrete attestation — the two pytest summary lines showing the suite passed with the expected test count — is absent from the ticket.
findings.remediation: Run the full test suite before and after the split, then record both pytest summary lines (e.g. '===== N passed in Xs =====') as a ticket comment, naming the commit SHA at which the run was performed and confirming the test count matches the pre-split baseline plus any new seam tests.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
